subject: nested model testing for measurement invariance

messages.subject: nested model testing for measurement invariance
parts:
Hello again Phil,

Thank you for the past advice, as well as any tips you could offer currently. I am (once again) looking at a large scale literacy assessment with 51 dichotomous and polytomous items. I have identified a bifactor model with a good fit to the data (yay). I am trying to run a series of nested models to identify the items/parameters where measurement invariance may be occurring between two groups.  Can you please confirm these are the steps?

CONFIGURAL: no restriction; adding "invariance=c('free_means', 'free_var'))" should be ok?

e.g., mod_configural <- multipleGroup(items, Q2, group = group1, 
                                invariance=c('free_means', 'free_var'))

METRIC/WEAK: "invariance=c('slopes'))"

e.g., mod_metric <- multipleGroup(items, Q2, group = group1, invariance=c('slopes')) 

STRONG/SCALAR:  invariance=c('slopes', 'intercepts', 'free_means')) 

e.g., mod_scalar <- multipleGroup(items, Q2, group = group1,
                            invariance=c('slopes', 'intercepts', 'free_means')) 

Here is where I had trouble. When I added "free_vars" to this it seemed to re-free the slopes/loadings across groups (e.g., it went back to configural and wasn't "nested" in the sense of becoming increasingly restrictive). Is it ok as is? 

STRICT: invariance=c('slopes', 'intercepts')) 

e.g., mod_strict <- multipleGroup(items, Q2, group = group1,
                            invariance=c('slopes', 'intercepts')) 

This is a naive/obvious question, but are the options listed above just broad strokes for the same function that CONSTRAINB does on individual items/parameters?

Lastly, after multigroup, do I need to run the DIF analyses separately for polytomous and dichotomous items, since they have a different number of d parameters?

Thanks!
Jeanne

On Tue, Jun 19, 2018 at 8:42 PM Jeanne Sinclair <jeanneh...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hello again Phil,

Thank you for the past advice, as well as any tips you could offer currently. I am (once again) looking at a large scale literacy assessment with 51 dichotomous and polytomous items. I have identified a bifactor model with a good fit to the data (yay). I am trying to run a series of nested models to identify the items/parameters where measurement invariance may be occurring between two groups.  Can you please confirm these are the steps?

CONFIGURAL: no restriction; adding "invariance=c('free_means', 'free_var'))" should be ok?

e.g., mod_configural <- multipleGroup(items, Q2, group = group1, 
                                invariance=c('free_means', 'free_var'))

This likely is not identified. Configural invariance is essentially completely independent (and independently identified) single group models; hence, if you took a subset of the data within each group and fit a model to that then the sum of the log-likelihood values would equal this config. Freeing the hyper mean/var parameters would only be possible if there are anchor items selected.

METRIC/WEAK: "invariance=c('slopes'))"

e.g., mod_metric <- multipleGroup(items, Q2, group = group1, invariance=c('slopes')) 

STRONG/SCALAR:  invariance=c('slopes', 'intercepts', 'free_means')) 

e.g., mod_scalar <- multipleGroup(items, Q2, group = group1,
                            invariance=c('slopes', 'intercepts', 'free_means')) 

Here is where I had trouble. When I added "free_vars" to this it seemed to re-free the slopes/loadings across groups (e.g., it went back to configural and wasn't "nested" in the sense of becoming increasingly restrictive). Is it ok as is? 

STRICT: invariance=c('slopes', 'intercepts')) 

e.g., mod_strict <- multipleGroup(items, Q2, group = group1,
                            invariance=c('slopes', 'intercepts')) 

This is a naive/obvious question, but are the options listed above just broad strokes for the same function that CONSTRAINB does on individual items/parameters?

Correct. I can't really confirm whether these are exact (the strict looks correct...groups are completely equal, even in terms of their latent trait distributions). IRT models don't perfectly fit this convention because there's really no such thing as a residual variance term (these parameters are not uniquely identified in IRT models compared to SEM, so that part falls out).
Lastly, after multigroup, do I need to run the DIF analyses separately for polytomous and dichotomous items, since they have a different number of d parameters?

Depends on your approach, such as via likelihood ratio tests, Wald tests, or even (finally) my DRF statistics:  https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11336-018-9626-9
But typically you isolate items one at a time and go from there, so via the automated DIF() function this could be a little more difficult (may require you to make two separate sweep runs, one for all dichotomous items then another for all related polytomous items). HTH.


Thanks!
Jeanne
